clue.text: Hold up the picnic basket

blocks.note: first meaning: to obstruct or impede
second meaning: a lidded wicker basket for food

explanation.surface: Someone is told to lift up the picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold up' reads as lifting the basket, but it is a verb meaning obstruct, a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for obstructing progress and a noun for a wicker container packed with food.

clue.text: Restraint shown by worker on strike

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece on another sits above it, so comes first

blocks.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
to cuff is to strike with the open hand

explanation.surface: A striking worker shows restraint on the picket line.
explanation.walkthrough: On strike suggests industrial action, but strike is a verb for a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Handcuffs are a pair of locked metal rings that restrain a prisoner's wrists.

clue.text: Food for team replacement at dinner-dance

indicators.note: a replacement swaps things around, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
a ball is a formal dance, often with dinner

explanation.surface: A substitute player is offered dinner at a formal dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A meatball is a small ball of minced meat, served as a dish, so an item of food.

clue.text: Number three is confused

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone muddles the number three.
explanation.walkthrough: Number is read as numb-er, something that numbs, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was an early anaesthetic gas that deadens feeling, so it is a numbing agent.

clue.text: Aim to put charged particle on circuit

indicators.note: to put one thing on another here means placing it after the other in an across entry

blocks.note: an ambit is a circuit or bounds
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: An instruction from a physics lab about sending a charged particle around a circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, A 'on' B puts A after B.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambition is a goal one strives toward, the same as an aim held in life.

clue.text: Young person has it at orgy - upset higher faction

indicators.note: in a down entry something upset is turned upside down, so read from the bottom

blocks.note: a minor is someone under the age of majority
taken as written
taken as written
up means higher

explanation.surface: A teenager at a wild party upsets a more senior group.
explanation.definitionFit: A minority group is a smaller faction within a population, set apart by politics, race or belief.

clue.text: In part, time will heal the affliction

indicators.note: in part means only a portion of the following words is taken

blocks.note: the letters run across the words from will into heal
the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A proverb-like comfort that time will partly heal suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through wILL HEAL THe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill health is a state of sickness or poor physical condition, which is an affliction.

clue.text: Damaged train at railway terminal where immediate  action is required

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so its letters are reordered
a terminal is the end point, so take the final letter only

blocks.note: taken as written
the end of this word

explanation.surface: A damaged train at the end of the line needs urgent attention.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-tray holds incoming papers on a desk, waiting for someone to deal with them promptly.

clue.text: Odd inclusion in study set-up - agreed?

indicators.note: in a down entry set up means raised, so the word is read bottom to top
an inclusion is something held inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a den is a private study room
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether everyone agrees to an odd addition in the study arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod is to signal yes with the head, so someone who nodded indicated assent.

clue.text: Down under in Wales

blocks.note: first meaning: poetic short form of beneath, below
second meaning: a town in south Wales

explanation.surface: Someone from Australia turns up in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' suggests Australia; here it just means beneath. Neath is a town near Swansea in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The poetic word 'neath, short for beneath, means below, and Neath is also a Welsh town name.

clue.text: Developing tendril, for example, is tightly curled

indicators.note: something developing changes its form, so the letters take a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written
e.g. abbreviates the Latin exempli gratia

explanation.surface: A botanical note that a growing tendril, for instance, coils tightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringlets are tight curls of hair, so something ringleted is formed into such close coils.

clue.text: Let the other guy pay back the fee

blocks.note: to back a car is to reverse it
a charge is a fee

explanation.surface: Someone is told to let another person cover the cost and repay the fee.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse-charge call is a phone call billed to the person receiving it, called collect in America.
explanation.definitionFit: To reverse the charge on a call makes the receiver, not the caller, pay for it.

clue.text: He takes the stand to get a fair deal, they say

definitions.text: He takes the stand to get a fair deal, they say

blocks.clueFragment: He takes the stand to get a fair deal, they say
blocks.note: surface reading: a witness going into the box in court hoping for justice

blocks.clueFragment: takes the stand to get a fair deal, they say
blocks.note: setter's reading: someone who waits at a taxi rank to pick up a fare, which sounds like fair

explanation.surface: A witness goes into the box hoping for justice.
explanation.walkthrough: The stand is a taxi rank, not the witness box, and 'they say' tells you fair is heard as fare, a passenger's payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi driver queues at a rank waiting to collect passengers who pay a fare for the ride.

clue.text: Scrub article written in Gaelic

indicators.note: something written in a language sits inside that language, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grammar item from a Gaelic text gets deleted.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan or record informally means to cancel or wipe it out, as to erase does.

clue.text: All choked up?

blocks.note: surface reading: overcome with emotion, tearful
setter's reading: a car engine with the choke or throttle opened all the way

explanation.surface: Someone is overcome with emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Choked suggests tears, but the choke and throttle are engine controls, and 'all' says the valve is fully open.
explanation.definitionFit: Full throttle means maximum engine power with the fuel valve open completely, hence top speed or maximum effort.

clue.text: Until now a mite shady, possibly, about one

indicators.note: possibly means the word is one possible arrangement of its letters
about means going around, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: a tot is a small child, like a mite
taken as written
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A child has seemed somewhat dubious up to the present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A mite' reads as 'slightly', modifying shady; it is a noun for a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means up to the present time, still continuing now, which is the sense of until now.

clue.text: Not rephrased, tune died out

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are not in their right order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A song fades away without its words being reworked.
explanation.definitionFit: Unedited text has not been revised or reworded by an editor, so it remains not rephrased.

clue.text: Fussy, cute sort gets the best of the meat

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange into a different order

blocks.note: prim means fussily proper
taken as written

explanation.surface: A finicky, pretty type of person gets the choicest meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cute sort' reads as a cute kind of person; sort is a verb to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime cut is a top-quality piece from a butchered carcass, the choicest portion.

clue.text: Power changed Rene into a strong supporter

indicators.note: a name that is changed has its letters rearranged

blocks.note: power and strength are synonyms
taken as written

explanation.surface: Power transforms a man called Rene into a sturdy champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A strengthener is a brace or reinforcement, something that supports a structure and makes it stronger.

clue.text: Top-up has modified a chemical compound

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read from the bottom
modified means altered, so the letters change order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A refill has altered a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: Top-up reads as a refill; split it into top and up.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is potassium carbonate or a related potassium salt, a compound used in fertilisers.

clue.text: A red desert?

blocks.note: first meaning: a dark brownish-red colour
second meaning: to abandon someone on an island

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a desert is red, like the outback.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert reads as a noun for sandy wastes; it is the verb to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Maroon is a shade of red, and to maroon someone is to abandon them somewhere isolated.

clue.text: Beast is all right and sounds happy

indicators.note: sounds tells us to go by how the words are spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: all right is okay, written OK
happy said with the h dropped, as in a Cockney accent

explanation.surface: An animal is said to be fine and content.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'okay 'appy' quickly, dropping the h, and you hear the name of the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest animal of central Africa related to the giraffe, a beast in the general sense.

clue.text: Monumental barrage put up by Mother with vacuum cleaner in front

indicators.note: in front says one piece goes before the other in the answer

blocks.note: Hoover is a brand name used in Britain for any vacuum cleaner
a dam is the mother of an animal

explanation.surface: Mum builds a huge wall with the help of her vacuum cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: Barrage is the French-derived word for a dam across a river, not gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hoover Dam is a vast concrete barrier on the Colorado River, a famous engineering monument.

clue.text: Get ready for battle - Marne, maybe

indicators.note: maybe signals that the word may be rearranged into another

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Troops prepare to fight at the Marne, the river of two great First World War battles.
explanation.definitionFit: Enarm is an archaic verb meaning to arm or equip with weapons, hence to prepare for fighting.

clue.text: A long way down to get an acceptable drink

blocks.note: first meaning: a long fall
second meaning: a wine worth drinking, in a connoisseur's phrase

explanation.surface: Someone travels far to find something decent to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop means both a fall and a small amount of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a considerable fall from a height, and is also the idiom for a pleasant glass of wine.

clue.text: "Room at the Top" showing in Athens

blocks.note: first meaning: a room under the roof of a house
second meaning: of Attica, the region around Athens

explanation.surface: The film Room at the Top is being screened in Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: Room at the Top is a 1959 British film, but here the words just describe a loft room. Attic as an adjective means Athenian.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the uppermost room under a roof, and Attic describes things of ancient Attica or Athens.

clue.text: Collector equipped with buzzer

blocks.note: surface reading: a debt or ticket collector carrying a doorbell or alarm
setter's reading: an insect that gathers nectar and makes a buzzing sound

explanation.surface: A rent collector arrives carrying an electric buzzer.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect gathers nectar and pollen from flowers and buzzes as it flies.

clue.text: Dicky admits being in the thick of it

definitions.note: a preposition with its object; the answer stands for 'in the thick of'

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or shaky, so the letters are unsound and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man named Dicky confesses he is caught up in the action.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a name; it is the British word for unreliable or weak, as in a dicky heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Amidst means surrounded by, among, which is being in the middle or busiest part of something.
